title: Shrimp Scampi Linguine
subtitle: plump garlic-butter shrimp with lemon and Parmesan, tossed through linguine in under 30 minutes
imageAlt: Linguine twirled with garlic butter shrimp and Parmesan in a white bowl with a lemon wedge on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the shrimp overnight in the fridge, or in a bowl of cold water 15 minutes. Peel and devein if needed; pat dry.
This moves fast: have everything chopped and measured before the pasta goes in.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the salt and cook the linguine until al dente. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

steps.title: Sear the shrimp
steps.text: Meanwhile, season the shrimp with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the shrimp in one layer 1–2 minutes a side, until pink, opaque and 74°C (165°F). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Garlic butter sauce
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium. Add 2 tbsp of the butter and the garlic and cook 1 minute without browning. Add the broth, lemon zest and juice and simmer 2–3 minutes to reduce by half.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the linguine, the remaining 2 tbsp butter, the Parmesan and a splash of pasta water and toss until glossy. Return the shrimp and their juices and toss 30 seconds to warm.

fixIt.fix: They overcooked. Take them out as soon as they curl into a C and turn opaque; they warm again at the end.
It browned. Cook it over medium, just until fragrant.
Toss hard with more pasta water; the starch brings the butter and Parmesan together.

saleTip: Frozen raw shrimp bags at No Frills go on sale for about $10; 31–40 size is the best value.
leftovers: Reheat gently with a splash of water; shrimp toughen if they boil.
doneness: Shrimp 74°C (165°F): pink and opaque all the way through (Health Canada, shellfish).
source: Based on tested shrimp scampi methods (America's Test Kitchen, Canadian Living): seared shrimp, garlic butter and lemon pan sauce, with chicken broth in place of white wine.
prepAhead: Peel and devein the shrimp up to 1 day ahead; keep them covered in the fridge.
reheat: Covered over low with a splash of water 3–4 minutes, or in the microwave 1–2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Garlic, butter and shrimp with linguine; no lemon zest or broth.

stepNotes.2: Basic: skip the broth and zest; use just the lemon juice and ½ cup of the pasta water.

fancy.note: Cherry tomatoes blistered in the pan and a crunchy garlic crumb.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: first toast the panko in the olive oil in the skillet over medium 3 minutes until golden; set aside and wipe the pan.
stepNotes.2: Fancy: add the cherry tomatoes with the garlic and cook 2 minutes until they soften.

addSteps.title: Crumb
addSteps.text: Scatter the garlic crumb over each bowl.

plating: Twirl the pasta high with tongs.
Crumb over the top, lemon wedge alongside.

why.1-0: Searing the shrimp first and returning them at the end keeps them tender.
why.1-6: Chicken broth stands in for the usual white wine and still gives the sauce body.
why.1-8: Parmesan and starchy pasta water turn the butter into a silky sauce.

funFact: 'Scampi' is the Italian name for langoustines; Italian-American cooks used shrimp instead and kept the name.

keeps.note: shrimp and butter sauces don't freeze well
